title: Clean invoice, exact PO match
story: Machine-readable PDF, explicit PO, quantities and prices match the PO exactly.

title: Inter-state freight, small variance within tolerance
story: Different layout, IGST instead of CGST/SGST, PO written as 'PO 2026/102'. The freight rate came in Rs.150/trip above the PO rate (+0.5%) - inside the 1% tolerance.

title: Tax embedded in prices
story: Small vendor quotes GST-inclusive rates. The process must back out the tax before comparing to the (pre-tax) PO.

title: One PO billed in parts (within balance)
story: Annual hosting PO billed quarterly. Q1 is already paid; this Q2 invoice uses 1 of the 3 remaining quarters.

title: Fax-quality scan, OCR misreads a digit
story: A faxed paper invoice with no text layer. The process OCRs it, then refuses to trust the OCR until the numbers reconcile. On this scan OCR reads CGST 8,676 as 6,676.
expect: APPROVE or REVIEW (depends on OCR quality)

title: Split PO - second invoice exceeds what's left
story: PO-2026-0104 was partly billed earlier (1,200 gloves + 300 goggles). This invoice bills 1,000 more gloves, but only 800 remain on the PO.

title: Duplicate re-sent in a different format
story: INV-0042 was already paid. The vendor re-sends it as a 'payment reminder' in a different layout and writes the number as 'INV42'. Same vendor, same amount, same PO.

title: No PO number on the invoice
story: The vendor forgot the PO reference. The process finds the most likely PO from vendor, items and amount - but does not auto-approve a guessed match.

title: Vendor is blocked in the master
story: Everything on the invoice is fine, but the vendor's KYC has expired, so payment must not go out.

title: Billed before all goods arrived
story: Kaveri bills 300 helmets on PO-2026-0110, but the warehouse has only received 200. Payment waits for the goods. The agent asks Stores; when they reply that the rest arrived, it books the receipt and re-checks.

title: Large vendor, no e-invoice (IRN)
story: Brightline is above the ₹5 crore e-invoicing limit but sent a plain PDF with no IRN. Without it the invoice isn't a valid tax invoice and ₹22,320 of input tax credit is lost. The agent asks the vendor for the e-invoice; when it arrives the IRN is checked against the invoice and payment is released (less 2% TDS on freight).

title: New layout: reviewer teaches it once
story: Nimbus switched billing systems. Its statement says 'Document Ref' and 'Dated', labels the reader has never seen, so the invoice number and date are missing. A reviewer types them in; the process finds them on the page, learns the labels for Nimbus, re-checks (the IRN confirms the typed number) and approves.
expect: REVIEW, then APPROVE after the correction

title: Same layout again: read automatically
story: The next Nimbus statement in the same layout. After #14 has been corrected once, the learned labels read it with no help. Before that, it needs a reviewer too.

title: Invoice in Hindi
story: A Delhi supplier's invoice with Hindi labels (बीजक संख्या, दिनांक, क्रय आदेश संख्या, कुल योग), Hindi tax names (आईजीएसटी) and dates in Devanagari digits. Same checks, same decision: no special path.

title: Real vendor, new bank account
story: A genuine-looking Sundaram invoice against a real open PO - everything matches, except it asks for payment to a NEW bank account. Classic business-email-compromise: hold and verify by phone.

title: Look-alike vendor, different bank
story: 'Sundaram Packaging Solution' (no s) with a different GSTIN and bank account, quoting Sundaram's real PO number. An impostor - payment must be frozen, and no reply sent that tips them off.
